# ResultCrafter

> A minimal, opinionated Result pattern library for modern .NET (8+). Provides `Result<T>`, `Result`, and `Error`
> as `readonly struct` types, with built-in RFC 9457 ProblemDetails pipeline, structured logging via
> `[LoggerMessage]`, first-class Minimal API support, and full MVC controller support.
> Ships as six focused NuGet packages under the `ResultCrafter.*` prefix. Current version: 2.0.0.

## Public namespaces

- `ResultCrafter`: the core primitives `Result`, `Result<T>`, `Error`, `ErrorType`, `SuccessKind`.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore`: Minimal API `To*Result` extensions, `Produces*` builder extensions, DI
  (`AddResultCrafter` / `UseResultCrafter`), `ResultCrafterOptions` / `ExceptionDetailMode`, exception handlers.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.Mvc`: controller `To*Result` extensions, `ProblemActionResult`, `Produces*Attribute` family.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.ProblemDetails`: `HttpErrorCatalog`, `ProblemDetailsBuilder`, enricher, keys, logger.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.EfCore`, `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation`, `ResultCrafter.FluentValidation`,
  `ResultCrafter.MediatR`: match their package IDs.

Code inside any `ResultCrafter.*` namespace resolves the core types without a `using` (parent namespace lookup);
consumers outside the library need `using ResultCrafter;`.

## Key design decisions

- `Result<T>`, `Result`, and `Error` are `readonly struct` — zero heap allocation on the success path.
- `ErrorType` enum starts at `None = 0` (sentinel). All factory methods on `Error` reject `None`, so
  `default(Error)` and `default(ErrorType)` are explicitly invalid rather than silently mapping to BadRequest.
- Both `Result<T>` and void `Result` carry a `SuccessKind` field (`Ok`, `Created`, `Accepted`, `NoContent`).
  Every `To*Result()` extension method, including `ToOkResult` and the typed `ToAcceptedResult`, on both the
  Minimal API and controller surfaces, validates that the `SuccessKind` matches the intended HTTP status code
  and throws `InvalidOperationException` on mismatch.
- `Result<T>.Map<TOut>(Func<T, TOut>)` transforms the success value while preserving `SuccessKind` and
  `Location`. On failure, the error propagates unchanged without invoking the selector.
- Success values are non-null by construction: `Result<T>.Ok`, `Created`, and `Accepted` throw
  `ArgumentNullException` on a null value, and `Map` throws `InvalidOperationException` when its selector
  returns null. Use the void `Result` for value-less success. `default(Result<T>)` bypasses the factories
  and is documented-invalid.
- Both result types expose `Match<TOut>(onSuccess, onFailure)` combinators. `IsSuccess` is annotated with
  `[MemberNotNullWhen(false, nameof(Error))]` (and, on `Result<T>`, `[MemberNotNullWhen(true, nameof(Value))]`)
  so neither `result.Error.Value` nor `result.Value` needs `!` after an `IsSuccess` check.
  Both carry a `[DebuggerDisplay]` for readable debugging.
- Error responses route through `IProblemDetailsService` on both the Minimal API and controller paths, so enrichment
  (instance, traceId, requestId) and 4xx structured logging fire from a single `IPostConfigureOptions` callback —
  `ConfigureResultCrafterProblemDetails` — with no per-path wiring.
- `ProblemDetailsBuilder` sets the RFC 9110 `type` URI explicitly via `HttpErrorCatalog.TypeUri()`, so the
  ProblemDetails object is self-describing at all stages of the pipeline.
- The exception handler uses `IExceptionHandler` (not custom middleware) so the try/catch cost is paid only when an
  exception actually occurs, not on every request.
- All log calls use `[LoggerMessage]` source generation; the 4xx path has an explicit `IsEnabled` guard to avoid
  string allocations when the log level is filtered.
- `ProblemActionResult` (controller path) sets `Response.StatusCode` from the mapped error and then calls
  `IProblemDetailsService.WriteAsync` inside `ExecuteResultAsync` (MVC leaves 200 for a custom ActionResult and
  the ProblemDetails service never copies `pd.Status` onto the transport), giving controllers identical
  pipeline behaviour to Minimal API endpoints.
- `GetInstance` returns `PathBase + Path` only (a valid RFC 9457 relative URI reference). The host is intentionally
  excluded — it breaks behind reverse proxies.
- `EfCoreConcurrencyExceptionHandler` is inserted *before* `ResultCrafterExceptionHandler` in the DI list so
  `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` resolves as 409 rather than falling through to 500; it sets the transport
  `Response.StatusCode` to 409 before writing (the exception-handler middleware has already set 500).
- `BadHttpRequestExceptionHandler` is registered by `AddResultCrafter()` *before* `ResultCrafterExceptionHandler` and
  maps a 4xx `BadHttpRequestException` (e.g. Minimal API binding failures, thrown only when
  `RouteHandlerOptions.ThrowOnBadRequest` is enabled — the Development default) to its carried status code rather than
  500, via the standard ProblemDetails pipeline, for dev/prod parity.
- `ConfigureResultCrafterProblemDetails` normalizes framework-default ProblemDetails (the binding handler above in
  Development, and bare status codes via `UseStatusCodePages` in Production) to the house style using
  `HttpErrorCatalog.TryGetErrorType`, only when the title is still the framework default — so a binding `400` reads
  `title: "bad_request"` identically in both environments, with Result-based and app-customized titles left intact.
- `ValidationFilter<T>` (in `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation`) aligns the field-error keys to the app's
  configured JSON `PropertyNamingPolicy` per path segment (camelCase by default) instead of mutating the global
  `ValidatorOptions.Global.PropertyNameResolver`, so `errors` keys match the wire JSON with no global side effect.
- `ResultCrafterMarker` + `ResultCrafterStartupValidator` enforce that both `AddResultCrafter()` and
  `UseResultCrafter()` are called; misconfiguration throws at startup, not at the first request.
- `ResultCrafter.MediatR` provides one open-generic behavior `ResultValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` covering
  both `Result` and `Result<T>` (and passing through other response types). A behavior that fixes `TResponse` to the
  void `Result` (arity 1) cannot be registered against the arity-2 `IPipelineBehavior<,>`, so the single fully-open
  behavior builds the failed response via a `ResultResponseFactory<TResponse>` delegate bound once per response type.
- MediatR validation behaviors execute validators sequentially (not `Task.WhenAll`) for safety with validators that
  depend on non-thread-safe scoped services (e.g. EF Core `DbContext`); failures are aggregated into one field-errors
  dictionary.
- `HttpErrorCatalog` switch expressions throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` on unrecognised `ErrorType` values
  (including `None`) rather than silently falling back to a default.

## Packages

- `ResultCrafter.Core` — primitives only, no framework dependencies.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore` — ProblemDetails pipeline, exception handler, Minimal API extensions, MVC controller
   extensions. Requires .NET 8+. Multi-targets net8.0;net9.0;net10.0.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.EfCore` — intercepts `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` -> 409. Call
  `AddResultCrafterEfCore()` after `AddResultCrafter()`.
- `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation` — `WithValidation<T>()` Minimal API endpoint filter plus the
  `AddResultCrafterValidation()` registration helper. Depends on `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore` + `ResultCrafter.FluentValidation`.
- `ResultCrafter.FluentValidation` — `ValidateToResultAsync` bridge from `IValidator<T>` to `Error.BadRequest`.
- `ResultCrafter.MediatR` — MediatR pipeline behaviors that run FluentValidation automatically for handlers returning
  `Result` / `Result<T>`, short-circuiting with `Error.BadRequest(fieldErrors)`.

## Source layout

### Core primitives (`src/ResultCrafter.Core/`, namespace `ResultCrafter`)

- [Error.cs](src/ResultCrafter.Core/Error.cs): `readonly struct`. Constructor rejects `ErrorType.None`.
  Factory methods: `NotFound`, `Unauthorized`, `Forbidden`, `Conflict`, `ConcurrencyConflict`, `Gone`,
  `UnprocessableEntity`, `TooManyRequests`, `BadRequest(string)`, `BadRequest(Dictionary<string,string[]>)`.
  `IsValidation` is true only when constructed with a field-errors dict. `BadRequest(errors)` copies the
  dictionary defensively with case-insensitive keys and merges (not overwrites) keys differing only by case.
- [Result.cs](src/ResultCrafter.Core/Result.cs): Void result with `SuccessKind` field. Factories:
  `NoContent` (Kind=NoContent), `Accepted` (Kind=Accepted), `Fail`. Implicit cast from `Error`.
  `Match<TOut>(Func<TOut> onSuccess, Func<Error, TOut> onFailure)`.
- [ResultT.cs](src/ResultCrafter.Core/ResultT.cs): `Result<T>` with `SuccessKind` field. Factories:
  `Ok`, `Created`, `Accepted` (all throw `ArgumentNullException` on a null value), `Fail`. Implicit cast
  from `T` and from `Error`. `Map<TOut>(Func<T, TOut>)` transforms the success value preserving Kind and
  Location and throws `InvalidOperationException` if the selector returns null.
  `Match<TOut>(Func<T, TOut> onSuccess, Func<Error, TOut> onFailure)`. `default(Result<T>)` is
  documented-invalid (bypasses the factories, reports success with a null `Value`).
- [ErrorType.cs](src/ResultCrafter.Core/ErrorType.cs): `None = 0` (sentinel), `BadRequest = 1`,
  `NotFound = 2`, `Conflict = 3`, `Unauthorized = 4`, `Forbidden = 5`, `ConcurrencyConflict = 6`,
  `Gone = 7`, `UnprocessableEntity = 8`, `TooManyRequests = 9`.
- [SuccessKind.cs](src/ResultCrafter.Core/SuccessKind.cs): `Ok`, `Created`, `Accepted`, `NoContent`.

### ASP.NET Core, DI wiring (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/`, namespace `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore`)

- [ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs):
  `AddResultCrafter()` — registers `AddProblemDetails`, `IPostConfigureOptions`, two `IExceptionHandler`s
  (`BadHttpRequestExceptionHandler` before the catch-all `ResultCrafterExceptionHandler`), `ResultCrafterMarker`,
  `ResultCrafterStartupValidator`.
- [ApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs):
  `UseResultCrafter()` — calls `UseExceptionHandler()` + `UseStatusCodePages()`, marks the sentinel.
- [ConfigureResultCrafterProblemDetails.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ConfigureResultCrafterProblemDetails.cs):
  `IPostConfigureOptions<ProblemDetailsOptions>` — enriches every response, logs 4xx, strips internal `x-rc`
  marker extensions.
- [ResultCrafterMarker.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ResultCrafterMarker.cs): Sentinel that
  tracks whether `UseResultCrafter()` was called.
- [ResultCrafterStartupValidator.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ResultCrafterStartupValidator.cs):
  `IHostedService` — throws `InvalidOperationException` at startup if the middleware was not registered.

### ASP.NET Core, Minimal API (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/`, namespace `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore`)

- [MinimalApiResultExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/MinimalApiResultExtensions.cs):
  `ToOkResult`, `ToCreatedResult`, `ToAcceptedResult`, `ToNoContentResult` return
  `Results<TSuccess, ProblemHttpResult>` typed unions for OpenAPI inference; `ToProblemResult` (on a bare
  `Error`) returns `ProblemHttpResult` directly. Every `To*Result` validates the `SuccessKind`
  (`ToOkResult` -> `Ok`, `ToCreatedResult` -> `Created`, `ToAcceptedResult` -> `Accepted`,
  `ToNoContentResult` -> `NoContent`) and throws `InvalidOperationException` on mismatch.
- [RouteHandlerBuilderExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/RouteHandlerBuilderExtensions.cs):
   `.ProducesBadRequest()`, `.ProducesUnauthorized()`, `.ProducesForbidden()`, `.ProducesNotFound()`,
   `.ProducesConflict()`, `.ProducesGone()`, `.ProducesUnprocessableEntity()`, `.ProducesTooManyRequests()`:
   OpenAPI documentation only, no runtime effect.

### ASP.NET Core, MVC controllers (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/Mvc/`, namespace `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.Mvc`)

- [ControllerResultExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/Mvc/ControllerResultExtensions.cs):
  `ToOkResult`, `ToCreatedResult`, `ToAcceptedResult`, `ToNoContentResult`, `ToProblemResult`: returns
  `ActionResult<T>` / `IActionResult`. Failure path returns `ProblemActionResult`. Same `SuccessKind`
  validation as Minimal API path.
- [ProblemActionResult.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/Mvc/ProblemActionResult.cs): `ActionResult` subclass. `ExecuteResultAsync` sets
  `Response.StatusCode` before writing, then calls
  `IProblemDetailsService.WriteAsync` (no fallback; a writer is always present because
  `AddResultCrafter()` guarantees `AddProblemDetails()` is registered). Enrichment, 4xx
   logging, and internal marker-extension stripping fire from `ConfigureResultCrafterProblemDetails`
   identically to the Minimal API path. No `Clone` helper or manual JSON fallback exists.
- [ControllersAttributes.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/Mvc/ControllersAttributes.cs):
  `[ProducesBadRequest]`, `[ProducesUnauthorized]`, `[ProducesForbidden]`, `[ProducesNotFound]`,
  `[ProducesConflict]`, `[ProducesGone]`, `[ProducesUnprocessableEntity]`, `[ProducesTooManyRequests]`:
  each inherits `ProducesResponseTypeAttribute<ProblemDetails>`, `AllowMultiple = true`.

### ASP.NET Core, ProblemDetails utilities (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ProblemDetails/`, namespace `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.ProblemDetails`)

- [ProblemDetailsBuilder.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ProblemDetails/ProblemDetailsBuilder.cs): Builds
  `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ProblemDetails` from `Error`. Sets `Type` (RFC 9110 URI), `x-rc` marker and
  `x-rc-error-id` extension keys; adds `errors` dict only when `error.IsValidation`.
- [HttpErrorCatalog.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ProblemDetails/HttpErrorCatalog.cs): `Status(ErrorType)`,
  `Title(ErrorType)`, `DefaultDetail(ErrorType)`, `TypeUri(ErrorType)`, `ResolveDetail(Error)`: pure switch
  expressions, no reflection. All throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` on `ErrorType.None`. Covers 400, 401,
  403, 404, 409 (Conflict and ConcurrencyConflict), 410 (Gone, title `gone`, default detail `resource_gone`),
  422 (UnprocessableEntity, title `unprocessable_entity`), 429 (TooManyRequests, title `too_many_requests`;
  type URI points at RFC 6585 section 4, the others at RFC 9110). `TryGetErrorType(int, out ErrorType)`
  reverse-maps 400/401/403/404/409/410/422/429 for house-style normalization (409 to generic `Conflict`).
- [ProblemDetailsEnricher.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ProblemDetails/ProblemDetailsEnricher.cs):
  `GetInstance(HttpContext)` -> `PathBase + Path` (relative URI, host excluded). `GetTraceId(HttpContext)` -> W3C
  activity ID. Both cached in `HttpContext.Items` with typed object keys. `Enrich(pd, ctx)` — does not overwrite
  existing values.
- [ProblemDetailsKeys.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ProblemDetails/ProblemDetailsKeys.cs): `x-rc` (marker,
  stripped before response), `x-rc-error-id` (error type string, stripped before response), `errors`
  (field-errors dict, kept in response).
- [ResultCrafterLogger.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ProblemDetails/ResultCrafterLogger.cs):
  `[LoggerMessage]` source-generated methods: `LogClientError` (level param, EventId 1), `LogUnhandledException`
  (Error level, EventId 2), `LogResponseAlreadyStarted` (Warning level, EventId 3).

### ASP.NET Core, Exception handling (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/`, namespace `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore`)

- [BadHttpRequestExceptionHandler.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/BadHttpRequestExceptionHandler.cs):
  `IExceptionHandler` — maps a 4xx `BadHttpRequestException` to its carried `StatusCode` through the ProblemDetails
  pipeline (sets the `x-rc` marker so the centralised 4xx logging + marker stripping fire). Registered before the
  catch-all; non-4xx or non-`BadHttpRequestException` fall through to `ResultCrafterExceptionHandler`.
- [ResultCrafterExceptionHandler.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ResultCrafterExceptionHandler.cs):
  `IExceptionHandler` — catches all unhandled exceptions, logs at Error, writes 500 ProblemDetails. Detail is
  sanitised in production (`ExceptionDetailMode.Auto` checks env name at startup using
  `OrdinalIgnoreCase` comparisons). Returns `false` if response has already started.

### ASP.NET Core, Options (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/`, namespace `ResultCrafter.AspNetCore`)

- [ResultCrafterOptions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore/ResultCrafterOptions.cs): `ExceptionDetailMode`
  (Auto/Sanitized/IncludeExceptionDetails), `DefaultServerErrorMessage`, `ClientErrorLogLevel`.

### EF Core integration (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.EfCore/`)

- [EfCoreConcurrencyExceptionHandler.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.EfCore/EfCoreConcurrencyExceptionHandler.cs):
  Handles `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` -> 409, setting the transport `Response.StatusCode` before writing.
  Inserted before `ResultCrafterExceptionHandler` in the DI registration list.
- [ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.EfCore/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs):
  `AddResultCrafterEfCore()`: locates the existing `ResultCrafterExceptionHandler` descriptor and inserts the EF
  Core handler before it. Throws if `AddResultCrafter()` was not called first.
- EF Core `PackageReference` floors are open minimums per TFM (8.0.0 / 9.0.0 / 10.0.0, no brackets), so
  consumers float to any later patch; the test project pins the latest patches to keep the repo build graph
  free of known-vulnerable transitives.

### FluentValidation integration (`src/ResultCrafter.FluentValidation/`)

- [ValidatorExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.FluentValidation/ValidatorExtensions.cs):
  `ValidateToResultAsync<T>` — returns `null` on success, `Error?` (a `BadRequest` with field-errors dict) on
  failure. Property names come from FluentValidation as-is; configure
  `ValidatorOptions.Global.PropertyNameResolver` for casing conventions.

### ASP.NET Core FluentValidation endpoint filter (`src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation/`)

- [ValidationFilter.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation/ValidationFilter.cs): `IEndpointFilter` —
  resolves `IValidator<TRequest>` from request services, runs `ValidateToResultAsync`, and on failure returns
  `error.ToProblemResult()` after re-keying the field errors with the configured JSON `PropertyNamingPolicy`
  (applied per path segment). Transparent pass-through when there is no matching `TRequest` argument; throws when a
  `TRequest` argument is present but no `IValidator<TRequest>` is registered (fail-fast).
- [ValidationFilterExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation/ValidationFilterExtensions.cs):
  `WithValidation<TRequest>()` for both `RouteHandlerBuilder` and `RouteGroupBuilder` — adds `ValidationFilter<TRequest>`
  and documents the `400` ProblemDetails response in OpenAPI.
- [ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs):
  `AddResultCrafterValidation(lifetime = Scoped, params assemblies)` — opt-in convenience that registers validators
  via FluentValidation's `AddValidatorsFromAssemblies`, defaulting to the calling assembly (`[MethodImpl(NoInlining)]`).

### MediatR integration (`src/ResultCrafter.MediatR/`)

- [ResultValidationBehavior.cs](src/ResultCrafter.MediatR/ResultValidationBehavior.cs):
  `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` — a single open behavior covering both `Result` and `Result<T>` responses
  (and a pass-through for any other response type). Runs all registered `IValidator<TRequest>` instances before the
  handler, aggregates failures, and returns the failed `Result`/`Result<T>` carrying `Error.BadRequest(fieldErrors)`.
  The failed-response factory is bound once per response type via `ResultResponseFactory<TResponse>` (no per-request
  reflection). Empty `PropertyName` is normalised to `"_"` using `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace`.
- [ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs](src/ResultCrafter.MediatR/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs):
  `AddResultCrafterValidation(this MediatRServiceConfiguration)` — registers the single open behavior with MediatR.

### Demo project (`tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/`)

- [Program.cs](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/Program.cs): Wires `AddResultCrafter`, `AddResultCrafterEfCore`,
  `AddControllers`, `ItemService` (Singleton), `AddResultCrafterValidation(ServiceLifetime.Singleton)` (Singleton
  because `ItemService` injects the validator; the library default is Scoped), and `AddMediatR` with
  `cfg.AddResultCrafterValidation()`. Mounts the Minimal API group at `/api`, the MediatR demo group at
  `/api/mediatr`, and controllers at `/api/ctrl`.
- [Mediatr.cs](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/Mediatr.cs): `GetItemQuery` (`IRequest<Result<ItemDto>>`) and
  `DeleteItemCommand` (`IRequest<Result>`) with their FluentValidation validators and handlers; the handlers
  only run when the pipeline behavior passes validation.
- [MapMediatRDemoEndpoints.cs](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/MapMediatRDemoEndpoints.cs): `MapMediatRDemoEndpoints`
  group extension: `GET /api/mediatr/items/{id}` (200/400/404) and `DELETE /api/mediatr/items/{id}` (204/400/404)
  dispatch through `IMediator.Send`, demonstrating the `ResultValidationBehavior` short-circuit end-to-end.
- [ItemEndpoints.cs](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/ItemEndpoints.cs): Minimal API endpoints covering all success kinds
  (Ok, Created, Accepted typed/void, NoContent) and all error types. `POST /items` uses
  `.WithValidation<CreateItemRequest>()`. Includes `/items/crash` (unhandled exception -> 500) and `/items/db-crash`
  (`DbUpdateConcurrencyException` -> 409).
- [ItemsController.cs](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/ItemsController.cs): MVC controller mirror
  of the Minimal API endpoints under `/api/ctrl/items`. Same `ItemService`, same result methods, attribute-based
  OpenAPI documentation. Includes `Crash()` and `DbCrash()` actions.
- [ItemService.cs](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/ItemService.cs): Thread-safe in-memory service using
  `ConcurrentDictionary` and `Interlocked.Increment`, exercising every Result/Error path.
- [ResultCrafter.Demo.http](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/ResultCrafter.Demo.http): HTTP request file with one request
  per status code for both Minimal API (`/api/items/*`) and controller (`/api/ctrl/items/*`) prefixes.

## Tests layout (`tests/ResultCrafter.Tests/`)

All tests use xUnit v3, running on Microsoft.Testing.Platform (`dotnet test` uses the MTP runner via
`global.json` `test.runner`). Test files mirror the source namespace they cover.

- `Core/`, with `ErrorTests`, `ResultVoidTests`, `ResultOfTTests`, `ResultDefaultAndMatchTests`: primitives,
  equality, implicit conversions, `ErrorType.None` sentinel, `SuccessKind` on void Result, `Map`, `Match`,
  and `default(Result)`/`default(Result<T>)` behaviour.
- `AspNetCore/`, with `DependencyInjectionTests`, `HttpErrorCatalogTests`, `HttpErrorCatalogReverseMapTests`,
  `ProblemDetailsBuilderTests`, `ProblemDetailsEnricherTests`, `BadHttpRequestExceptionHandlerTests`,
  `ValidationFilterTests`, `TransportStatusCodeTests`, `SuccessKindGuardTests`, `EfCoreHandlerOrderingTests`:
  pipeline wiring, status/title/detail/typeUri mapping (including the `TryGetErrorType` reverse map), enrichment
  caching, `ErrorType.None` rejection, the `BadHttpRequestException` 4xx mapping, the `WithValidation<T>()`
  endpoint filter, transport-level `Response.StatusCode` correctness, the `SuccessKind` mismatch guards on every
  `To*Result` method, and EF Core handler ordering before the catch-all 500 handler. Handler/filter tests run
  against an in-memory `TestServer` (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost`) via the `TestApp` helper. The controller
  tests live in this same flat directory: `ControllerResultExtensionsTests`, `ProblemActionResultTests`
  (using a `CapturingProblemDetailsService` spy), `ControllerResultAttributesTests`.
- `FluentValidation/`, with `ValidatorExtensionsTests`: null on success, field-errors dict on failure.
- `MediatR/`, with `ResultValidationBehaviorTests`, `VoidResultValidationBehaviorTests`, `MediatRRegistrationTests`:
  validator pass-through, aggregation (including blank-message filtering and dedup), cancellation token flow,
  and open-behavior registration.

## Extension points and conventions

- To add a new `ErrorType`: add the enum value in `ErrorType.cs` (explicit int value), add a factory on `Error`,
  add `Status`/`Title`/`DefaultDetail`/`TypeUri` cases in `HttpErrorCatalog` (plus a `TryGetErrorType`
  reverse-map case when bare responses with that status should be normalized to the house style), add the
  `ProducesXxx` attribute in `Mvc/ControllersAttributes.cs` and the builder extension in
  `RouteHandlerBuilderExtensions.cs`.
- Never add per-request host resolution to `GetInstance` — it must remain a relative URI for proxy safety.
- `x-rc` and `x-rc-error-id` are internal pipeline markers. They are always stripped before the response is
  written. Do not document them as public API.
- Both `IProblemDetailsService.WriteAsync` and `TryWriteAsync` exist. Use `WriteAsync` when a
  writer is guaranteed (i.e. inside ResultCrafter, where `AddResultCrafter()` always calls
  `AddProblemDetails()`). Use `TryWriteAsync` only when a fallback is needed if no writer is
   registered. `WriteAsync` delegates to `TryWriteAsync` internally and throws
   `InvalidOperationException` if no writer handled the context.

- [README.md](README.md): Full usage documentation, alternatives comparison, configuration reference, performance
  notes.
- [ResultCrafter.Demo.http](tests/ResultCrafter.Demo/ResultCrafter.Demo.http): Run the demo project then execute
  requests directly in JetBrains Rider, VS Code REST Client, or any `.http`-compatible tool.
